Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

happen verb

to do something, by chance

also happen to, by chance, as it happens, do you happen to know?, if by any chance, accidentally, by accident, I just happened to see him

classical

Hor. S. 1.9.1: ībam forte viā Sacrā
Cic. Planc. 65: Puteolōs forte vēnissem (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 289
Traupman 325

1forte: short final e (Lewis & Short fortē). The ablative of the third-declension fors (de Vaan 236, s.v. fors: “abl. forte ‘by chance’”). Verg. A. 1.377, forte suā Libycīs tempestās adpulit ōrīs, and Hor. S. 1.9.1, ībam forte viā Sacrā: in both, forte su- and forte vi- are dactyls.

forte1

adverb (the ablative of fors)

by chance, as it happened

Latin says “I happened to …” with the verb and forte: forte vīdī, I happened to see. Sī forte, if by any chance; nisi forte, unless perhaps; forte fortūnā, by sheer luck (Ter. Eun. 134, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • cāsū — by chance, by accident

    adverb (the ablative of cāsus) · also used · classical · Cic. Planc. 65: cum cāsū diēbus iīs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 60: cāsū cecidī, I fell accidentally; Traupman 289

    Often beside forte; the opposite is cōnsiliō, on purpose.

Examples

  • Ībam forte viā Sacrā, sīcut meus est mōs

    I happened to be walking along the Sacred Way, as is my habitHor. S. 1.9.1

  • erat forte brūmae tempus et nivālis diēs

    it happened to be midwinter, and a snowy dayLiv. 21.54.7

  • ut vēlōcissimus quoque, sī forte iter cum parvulō faciat, det manum et gradum suum minuat

    as even the fastest walker, if he happens to be travelling with a little child, gives him his hand and shortens his stepQuint. 2.3.7

  • Forte eum cōnspexī.

    I just happened to spot him.Traupman 325

See also happen, perhaps, chance, opportunity.
